### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Fills the ghosts of a layout-owned face from the neighbouring block: a raw copy on a slab
layout, and on the cubed sphere an optional interpolation of the received strip followed by a rotation of
the vector components into the receiving panel's frame; corners are synthesized from the edge strips.
**Switch.** `SyncOptions`: `interpolate` (default off), `skip_corner` (default on), `type`, `dim`,
`intra_panel_only`, `cross_panel_only`.
**Requires / implies / turns off.** The hydro and scalar state exchanges set `interpolate` on; the donor
factor of the positivity limiter is exchanged raw.
**Order.** An exact copy on matched cells; the corner average preserves constants; no seam order is measured.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch11-exchange-corner.
:::

This is a pointer section: the interpolation weights and the coordinate transforms belong to @sec-ch03, and
the communication scheduling, buffers and tags belong to @sec-ch14. What is derived here is the one identity
the layout itself implements, the corner synthesis, together with the ownership facts the boundary chapter
relies on: which exchanges interpolate, which do not, and when the corners are filled.

### Derivation

The directly implemented corner identity is the arithmetic average of two edge strips. For generic values
$q$ already in the destination frame,

$$
q^{\mathrm{corner}}=\tfrac12\bigl(q^{\mathrm{edge1}}+q^{\mathrm{edge2}}\bigr).
$$ {#eq-ch11-exchange-corner}

`LayoutImpl::fill_corners` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::fill_corners >}}) implements
@eq-ch11-exchange-corner for the four corners of the tangential plane by broadcasting the end rows of the
two adjacent exchanged strips. The weights sum to one, so constants are preserved exactly in real arithmetic;
this does not prove a two-dimensional interpolation order. Check C4 checks the constant-preservation identity
and records why nonconstant edge values need not reconstruct the corner value [check
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`]. The checks
do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

`LayoutImpl::finalize` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::finalize >}}) waits for the
point-to-point work, deserializes the received strips, and calls `fill_corners` once per exchange when
`skip_corner` is on and the exchange is not one half of a split cubed-sphere sync. On the cubed sphere the
interpolated exchange of a subdivided panel runs in two halves, intra-panel first and cross-panel second, so
that the widened donor strip of a panel seam already holds its tangential halo. `CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize`
({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize >}}) writes the received
strip, calls the coordinate's `interp_ghost` when `interpolate` is on, and then rotates the three velocity
or momentum rows for `kConserved` and `kPrimitive` input; `kScalar` input is copied as is.
`GnomonicEquiangleImpl::interp_ghost` ({{< code src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp GnomonicEquiangleImpl::interp_ghost >}})
interpolates the strip widened by `cs_interp_margin` along the panel edge. The hydro state is exchanged
with `interpolate` on in the stage and initialization exchanges of @sec-ch11-timing; the donor factor of the
flux positivity limiter is exchanged raw, `interpolate(false)` with scalar type, in `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), because the donor of a seam face is the
neighbour's edge cell and an interpolated ghost is not its factor. This is a data-ownership map; no measured
seam order is claimed.

@fig-ch11-exchange-stencil illustrates the operations, with labelled roles independent of colour.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch11-exchange-stencil
#| fig-cap: "Supply ghosts through layout exchange. Schematic only; no simulation measurements."
#| fig-alt: "Labelled schematic of the exchange boundary operation; ghosts and owned cells have separate text labels."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch11.fig_exchange_stencil import make_fig
```

: Implementation sites for exchange. {#tbl-ch11-exchange-code}

1. Read the sync flags; the defaults do not interpolate and do skip corners. The anchor `skip_corner` is in
   {{< code src/layout/layout.hpp SyncOptions >}}.
2. For the subdivided interpolated panel path, finish the intra-panel exchange before packing the
   cross-panel donors. The anchor `interpolate` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}.
3. Deserialize, interpolate when selected, transform the vector components, and synthesize the corners once
   per exchange. The anchor `interp_ghost` is in
   {{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::deserialize >}}; the anchor
   `fill_corners` is in {{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::finalize >}}.
4. Keep the raw scalar donor-factor exchange separate from the interpolated hydro exchange. The anchor
   `interpolate` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.

{{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block >}}.

The neighbour assertion is the top-level `assert` in {{< code tests/test_mesh_exchange.py >}}.

Numeric tolerances above are the source test constants; a round-off derivation is not documented for each.
Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch15-ch11.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The corner average is not the panel-edge interpolation formula. The CPU/CUDA equality assertions of the
panel suite do not establish multi-process coverage. The vertical-velocity exchange suite checks its own
`ideal_match` criterion ({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py main >}}); no result
is claimed without a run. Broader seam flux and positivity coverage belongs to @sec-ch03 and
@sec-ch12-matrix.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
